anzsic_codes.name: Cheese and Other Dairy Product Manufacturing

merger_description:
B.S.A. SAS (together with its subsidiaries, **Lactalis**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of Saputo Dairy UK Ltd (together with its subsidiaries, **Saputo Dairy UK**) from Saputo Foods Limited, which is wholly-owned by Saputo Inc. (**Saputo**) (the **Acquisition**).

Lactalis is a privately held dairy group headquartered in Laval, France. Lactalis is active worldwide, manufacturing or supplying dairy products across six main categories: cheese, drinking milk, chilled dairy products, chilled yellow spreads, cream and dairy ingredients. Lactalis also manufactures or supplies other products, including drinks, charcuterie, frozen products, confectionery and desserts.

In Australia, Lactalis primarily supplies dairy products, including drinking milk, flavoured milk, iced coffee beverages, yoghurt, chilled yellow spreads, cream and cheese. Its portfolio includes a number of Australian brands (including Pauls, OAK, Ice Break, Jalna, Vaalia, Tamar Valley, Lemnos, Jindi, Harvey Fresh, Western Star, Mainland and Perfect Italiano) and international brands (including Président and Galbani).

Saputo Inc. is a Canadian dairy company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, and one of the largest dairy processors in the world. Saputo Dairy UK is a manufacturer of branded cheese and dairy spreads in the UK. It has no manufacturing facilities in Australia.

In Australia, Saputo Dairy UK operates in the wholesale supply of two cheese products: (i) a plant-based cheese product (which is supplied as a finished consumer product on a wholesale basis); and (ii) Wensleydale cheese (a UK territorial cheese).

Saputo Dairy Australia Pty Ltd (**Saputo Dairy Australia**), which produces, markets and distributes dairy products (including under the consumer brands, Cheer, Cracker Barrel, and Mersey Valley) is not a party to this Acquisition. Saputo Dairy UK supplies a plant-based cheese product to Saputo Dairy Australia under its own Cheer brand.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition may raise competition issues given:
a. there is horizontal overlap between Lactalis and Saputo
Dairy UK in the supply of cheese (including speciality
cheeses) to wholesalers in Australia
b. Lactalis is a major provider of dairy products in
Australia, including the wholesale supply of cheese
c. the relevant markets are unclear and the extent to which
the merged entity is likely to be constrained by
alternative suppliers is uncertain
d. the extent to which the Acquisition would reduce
competition between Lactalis and Saputo in Australia is
unclear.
The ACCC considers that these potential competition issues warrant
consideration through the notification process, including via
consultation with third parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
Given the above, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to reach a
concluded view on the likelihood of the Acquisition meeting the
notification thresholds. However, the ACCC notes that based on the
information provided in the application, the Acquisition may meet
the notification threshold in section 2-1 of the Competition and
Consumer (Notification of Acquisitions) Determination 2025.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
